title: Altair-Nidhogg: Which Model-Merging Theories Hold for a One-Pass Decision Encoder? Soups, Task Arithmetic, TIES and DARE Against Joint Training and Prediction Ensembling
abstract: arXiv:2611.27550v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Laya is a small model that answers a multiple-choice question in one pass: each option has a name and a written description. A new skill costs a training run, so we test whether published recipes for merging fine-tuned models (weight averaging, task arithmetic, TIES, DARE) work for it, and whether the theories behind them hold. All 156 models start from one released checkpoint: four plain fine-tunes, five specialists (each adds one kind of training row), joint fine-tunes on all rows, and prediction ensembles. Items are held-out, synthetic and LLM-labelled. In-family, each skill is scored on new items of its own kind, and "kept" is the share of a specialist's gain over the plain fine-tune. Averaging four specialists keeps 52% [38, 64] with +1.7 points of general accuracy; adding the full vectors keeps 42% [3, 63] with -9.0; TIES, which trims and resolves sign conflicts, keeps 64% [50, 76] with +1.5; joint fine-tunes, which see all the row

translated_title: Altair-Nidhogg：哪些模型合并理论适用于单次前向决策编码器？模型汤、任务算术、TIES 与 DARE 对比联合训练与预测集成
translated_abstract: arXiv:2611.27550v1 公告类型：新 摘要：Laya 是一个小型模型，可以在一次前向传播中回答多项选择题：每个选项都有一个名称和一段文字描述。学习一项新技能需要一次额外的训练运行，因此我们测试已发表的微调模型合并配方（权重平均、任务算术、TIES、DARE）是否对它有效，以及这些配方背后的理论是否成立。全部 156 个模型都从同一个已发布的检查点出发：四个普通微调模型、五个专家模型（每个增加一种训练数据行）、在所有数据行上的联合微调模型，以及预测集成模型。测试项目均为保留项目、合成项目并由大语言模型标注。在同一家族内，每项技能都在其自身类型的新项目上评分，“保留率”指专家模型相对于普通微调的增益中被保留的比例。对四个专家模型进行平均可保留 52% [38, 64] 的增益，同时通用准确率提升 1.7 分；添加完整任务向量可保留 42% [3, 63]，但通用准确率下降 9.0 分；通过修剪并解决符号冲突的 TIES 可保留 64% [50, 76]，同时通用准确率提升 1.5 分；能够看到所有数据行的联合微调……
tldr: 该论文在一个单次前向决策编码器上系统检验了模型汤、任务算术、TIES 和 DARE 四种模型合并配方是否有效及其理论是否成立，发现 TIES 对专家增益的保留率最高（64%），并将其与联合训练和预测集成进行了全面对比。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically tests whether model soups, task arithmetic, TIES and DARE work for a one-pass decision encoder and whether their underlying theories hold, finding that TIES retains the highest share (64%) of specialist gains when compared against joint training and prediction ensembling.
